prompt: Find the two most frequent words in an array, breaking frequency ties alphabetically; pad the result with null when there are fewer than two distinct words.
explanation: This is the count-then-rank pattern: a HashMap tallies frequencies in one pass, then the distinct words are sorted by a two-level comparator -- count descending first, alphabetical order as the tie-breaker. Writing counts.get(y) - counts.get(x) (y before x) flips the sort to descending. Guarding the array fills with size checks handles zero or one distinct word, leaving nulls from the freshly allocated String[2].
hints: First build a HashMap<String, Integer> of word counts with getOrDefault(word, 0) + 1.
Copy counts.keySet() into an ArrayList and sort it with a comparator: higher count first, then compareTo for ties.
counts.get(y) - counts.get(x) sorts by descending count; after sorting, take element 0 and (if present) element 1.
